sentiment.label: risk_off
sentiment.reason_it: Il mercato mostra segnali di cautela con il VIX a 16.18 (+7.65%) e il prezzo del petrolio in aumento (+2.54%). La situazione geopolitica rimane tesa, con la guerra tra USA-Israele e Iran al centro dell'attenzione. I dati macroeconomici mostrano un'inflazione ancora alta, con il CPI YoY USA al 4.3%. Le banche centrali, come la BCE e la Fed, sono in attesa di ulteriori sviluppi prima di prendere decisioni sui tassi. Secondo BlackRock e Goldman Sachs, le prospettive per il mercato sono incerte, con un possibile impatto negativo sulla crescita economica.
sentiment.reason_en: The market shows signs of caution with the VIX at 16.18 (+7.65%) and the oil price rising (+2.54%). The geopolitical situation remains tense, with the war between the USA, Israel, and Iran at the center of attention. Macroeconomic data shows high inflation, with the US YoY CPI at 4.3%. Central banks, such as the ECB and the Fed, are waiting for further developments before making decisions on interest rates. According to BlackRock and Goldman Sachs, the outlook for the market is uncertain, with a possible negative impact on economic growth.

I report settimanali di BlackRock e Goldman Sachs sottolineano l'incertezza del mercato e il possibile impatto negativo sulla crescita economica.
market_impact_summary.en: The stock market shows signs of weakness, with the S&P 500 at 7575.39 (+0.42%) and the NIKKEI at 67,243 (-1.92%). The oil price is rising, with BRENT at $77.94 (+2.54%). The geopolitical situation and macroeconomic data are influencing the market, with central banks waiting for further developments. The weekly reports from BlackRock and Goldman Sachs highlight the market's uncertainty and the possible negative impact on economic growth.

audio_script_it:
Buongiorno, benvenuti al Morning Briefing di Price Alert.

Il Nikkei ha chiuso in calo dell'1,92%, Shanghai in calo del 2,06%. Questo suggerisce un'apertura debole per i mercati europei.

Il S&P 500 è in rialzo dello 0,42% a settimila cinquecentosettantasette punti, il VIX sale del 7,65% a sedici virgola diciotto, segnale di volatilità crescente. Il Dollar Index è in lieve ribasso dello 0,08% a cento virgola ottantanove, mentre l'EUR/USD resta stabile al 1,14. Il rendimento del US 10Y è in rialzo dello 0,66% a quattro virgola cinquantasei per cento, riflettendo aspettative di inflazione più alte. Il TLT 20Y è pressoché invariato, -0,02%. L'oro scende del 0,65% a quattro mila settantasette dollari l'oncia, pressione al ribasso legata al dollaro più forte. Il Brent guadagna del 2,54% a settantasette dollari e novantaquattro centesimi, spinto da tensioni geopolitiche. Il BTP 10Y resta stabile al 3,82%.

Sul fronte geopolitico, il summit NATO inizia oggi a Washington, con discussioni su supporto all'Ucraina e coordinamento delle sanzioni contro la Russia; le decisioni potrebbero influenzare i prezzi dell'energia. Inoltre, il commento di Otmar Issing, padre dell'euro, sottolinea che guerra e inflazione porteranno BCE e Fed a una stretta collaborazione, rafforzando la percezione di un contesto di rischio off.

Nessun dato macro rilevante in uscita oggi.

Passiamo ora al comparto degli asset digitali. Bitcoin registra una discesa dell'1,31% e si attesta a sessantatré mila trentadue dollari. Gli ETF registrano un afflusso netto di novanta virgola quattro milioni di dollari, segnale di interesse istituzionale nonostante la pressione ribassista. Inoltre, notizie di mercato indicano che Bitcoin rimane vicino a sessantatré ottocento dollari, con vendite legate a conflitti globali che colpiscono altri asset ma non la cripto. Sentiment del mercato mostra un indice Fear & Greed a ventotto, classificato come paura, suggerendo cautela tra gli investitori.

Nessun dato macro in agenda oggi. Per approfondire i temi di oggi, sulla nostra piattaforma trovate gli articoli completi nella sezione Storie in Primo Piano. Grazie per l'attenzione e a domani. Continuate a seguirci per le prossime analisi di mercato. Restate aggiornati sui movimenti dei titoli e sulle opportunità di investimento.
audio_script_en:
Good morning, welcome to the Price Alert Morning Briefing.

The Nikkei closed down 1.92%, Shanghai down 2.06%. This suggests a weak opening for European markets.

The S&P 500 is up 0.42% at 6,527 points, the VIX up 7.65% at 16.18, signaling rising volatility. The Dollar Index is slightly lower 0.08% at 100.89, while EUR/USD remains stable at 1.14. The US 10Y yield is up 0.66% at 4.56%, reflecting higher inflation expectations. The TLT 20Y is essentially flat, -0.02%. Gold falls 0.65% to $4,777 per ounce, pressure from a stronger dollar. Brent gains 2.54% to $77.94, driven by geopolitical tensions. The BTP 10Y stays stable at 3.82%.

On the geopolitical front, the NATO summit kicks off today in Washington, with talks on support for Ukraine and coordination of sanctions against Russia; decisions could affect energy prices. Moreover, Otmar Issing, the father of the euro, notes that war and inflation will push the ECB and Fed into tighter cooperation, reinforcing a risk‑off environment.

No significant macro data scheduled for release today.

Let's pivot to the cryptocurrency markets... Bitcoin is down 1.31% and sits at $33,232. ETFs see a net inflow of $90.4 million, a sign of institutional interest despite bearish pressure. Market news also shows Bitcoin hovering near $33,800, with sell‑offs linked to global conflicts hitting other assets but not crypto. Market sentiment shows a Fear & Greed index at 28, classified as fear, suggesting caution among investors.

No macro data on the agenda today. For deeper coverage of today's topics, visit our platform for the full articles in the Featured Stories section. Thank you for listening and see you tomorrow. Keep following us for upcoming market analyses. Stay updated on stock movements and investment opportunities.

articles.title: An Unlearned Lesson: The Sorry Record of Regime Change Operations in the Middle East
articles.snippet: On Feb. 28, 2026, President Donald Trump announced the commencement of Operation Epic Fury, a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation against Iran. Among the mission’s goals was the overthrow of the Islamic Republic. “When we are finished,” Trump told the Iranian people, “take over your government. It will be yours to take.” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu echoed Trump’s message, saying: “Our joint action will create the conditions for the brave Iranian people to take their destiny into their own hands.” To be sure, Washington and Jerusalem had other objectives — above all, preventing the Islamic Republic from acquiring nuclear weapons The post An Unlearned Lesson: The Sorry Record of Regime Change Operations in the Middle East appeared first on War on the Rocks .

articles.title: Are Trump administration policies catalyzing European unity?
articles.snippet: The second Trump administration has signaled occasional hostility to Europeans and the European Union in ways unprecedented in American government practice since the beginnings of European integration in the 1950s. articles.title: Big Oil’s War-Related Profits Anger Governments
articles.snippet: Supermajors are set to report bumper profits for the second quarter thanks to the surge in oil and gas prices, driven higher by the hostilities between the United States, Israel, and Iran. This is a problem for governments—notably the Trump administration, but politicians in Europe are angry at Big Oil’s good fortune again. Oil prices soared fourfold earlier this year after U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran prompted the latter to shut traffic via the Strait of Hormuz—something Tehran had been threatening it would do for decades…
